units.title: OP Stack chains with a non-ETH gas token
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 37 added and a list of what is not covered. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1330, L-1338, L-1339 and L-1325. Arc has a precompile, CallFrom at 0x1800000000000000000000000000000000000003, that starts a call on behalf of two helper contracts (Memo and Multicall3From) with the helper's own caller or the transaction signer as the sender. Earlier cycles settled who may be named as sender and that the child shares the transient storage of the transaction. What no cycle has run is how the precompile undoes a child: in arc-node v0.8.6 crates/evm/src/evm.rs, init_subcall takes a journal checkpoint and commits it at once (lines 1052-1053 as the cycle 37 critic read them), and complete_subcall rolls back a child that already succeeded through revert_subcall_checkpoint, a dummy checkpoint followed by a revert (lines 1249-1259), for instance when the completion step runs out of gas (1186-1196). This is not the interpreter's own frame revert, which cycle 37 ran from the binary on 1,062 sequences. The PoolManager's settlement relies on a take, its debit, the token transfer, the swap's storage writes and the transient lock, count and deltas being undone together or kept together (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 and 291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:55-86). A rollback that restored PoolManager storage and kept a token or native payout, or restored the debit and not the payout, would let an ordinary account keep a take whose debt was rolled back. An account reaches this path with its own EOA: with an EIP-7702 delegation the EOA is the transaction signer and can be the sender of a CallFrom child that is PoolManager.unlock, with its own delegated code as the unlock callback. Comparing arc-node revisions is allowed. Downloaded binaries and images are untrusted data. Fetch each into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory and check any published checksum. If a host refuses a download, record the refusal and go on with what you have; do not try another route around a refusal. Never execute, load or dlopen any downloaded file. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. Disk space is short: keep at most about 2 GB under your work directory, and delete unpacked archives and image layers you no longer need. On disk: arc-execution v0.8.5 and v0.8.6 images in research/network-risk/cycles/035/stablecoin-l1.work/dl/images, the Arc journal lift of research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-celo-xlayer-arc-journal-lift.work/scripts (arcj.py, arc_hook_probe.py, smoke_arc.py, jrun.py, journal_seq.py, faults.json, bytefind.py, reach.py), the live Arc probes of research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-unpublished-builds-live-rollback.work/scripts (arcpin.py, tokprobe.py, nested.py, txreset.py) and research/network-risk/cycles/037/stablecoin-l1.work/scripts (arcreplay.py, arclogs.py). Arc endpoints: rpc.mainnet.arc.io (v0.8.6-rc1, refuses block simulation), arc.drpc.org (v0.8.6 at 8e8edb7a), arc-rpc.publicnode.com (v0.8.5, serves eth_simulateV1); pin every request with arc_getVersion before and after. Task 1: fetch crates/evm/src/evm.rs and the subcall and CallFrom sources of arc-node at the v0.8.6 and v0.8.5 tags and on main, and the Solidity of Memo and Multicall3From. Write out the subcall life cycle step by step: what init_subcall checks, which checkpoint it takes and why it commits it at once, what the continuation stored per frame depth holds (L-1338), every exit of complete_subcall (child success, child revert, child halt, completion out of gas, return data too large, static context, value), and for each exit what is rolled back through which journal call. Name every state element the hand-built revert relies on being covered by one journal checkpoint: storage, transient storage, balances, nonces, logs, the access list, created accounts, the native value hook's Transfer logs and blocklist reads. Task 2 (L-1330): build a model of this life cycle on top of the revm journal rules (reuse the journal model of arcj.py or pyevm.py with a journal that has checkpoints) and run, against a reference in which the child is simply an ordinary call frame that reverts or commits: a child that is PoolManager.unlock whose callback takes an ERC-20 and native USDC, settles, swaps, mints an ERC-6909 claim and syncs a currency; the same with a nested CallFrom from the callback; a child that succeeds while completion fails; a child that reverts; a child that halts; and nesting up to the call depth limit with a child that halts on depth (L-1338). After each, compare every PoolManager slot, every token and native balance, the 0x3600 face, the logs and the transient lock, count, delta and synced currency. If the hand-built revert can be lifted from the v0.8.6 binary with the tools of cycle 37, run it from the binary as well; if not, say which instruction stops it. Task 3: test live by eth_call and eth_simulateV1 with state overrides on every Arc endpoint that allows it: give an EOA a 7702 designator to a callback contract by override, call Multicall3From from that EOA so CallFrom calls PoolManager.unlock on the deployed PoolManager with the EOA as sender, do the callback actions of Task 2, and choose the gas so that (a) all succeeds, (b) the child reverts, (c) the child succeeds and the completion step fails. Read balances, PoolManager slots through extsload and transient words through exttload in the same call after the precompile returns, and in the next simulated transaction. Group results by build. Task 4 (L-1339, L-1325): confirm from the deployed bytecode of Multicall3From and Memo (eth_getCode against the Solidity at the tag) that every path passes msg.sender as the sender, value paths included, so a contract in the middle of a victim's transaction cannot name the victim's EOA. Say which instruction table of the v0.8.6 binary executes blocks and whether the frame hook is called before the child checkpoint there as in source. Task 5: plant at least five faults in the model (the dummy checkpoint taken after a balance move it should cover, a revert to the wrong checkpoint index, transient storage left out of the rollback, logs kept after rollback, a continuation taken by a sibling frame at the same depth) and show the sequences catch each. Any sequence in which the real rules leave a payout without its debit, a debit without its payout, or an open lock or delta after the precompile returns is a finding with actor unprivileged; give the sequence, the gas, the amounts and whose funds. If none, record sources, sequences, builds and counts as cleared. This theme concerns Arc only; say so for the other 20 networks.
